BiblicalUsage: Korem is a vinedresser, a keeper of vines. 2 Kings 25:12 and Jeremiah 52:16 leave the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen when Jerusalem falls, 2 Chronicles 26:10 has Uzziah's husbandmen and vinedressers in the mountains and in Carmel, Isaiah 61:5 says the sons of the alien shall be your plowmen and your vinedressers, and Joel 1:11 cries, howl, O ye vinedressers, for the wheat and the barley, because the harvest of the field is perished.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the vinedresser is the man left behind: the poor of the land kept to tend the vines when the city fell, and the strangers shall tend them when it rises. I hold that Joel's howling vinedresser is the honest one, because he mourns the harvest instead of pretending it did not perish.
